name: wget
description: A non-interactive network downloader designed for robust downloads: retries, resume, mirroring, and background operation.

flags.description: Write to a specific file (-O - for stdout).
Quiet mode; -q --show-progress shows a bar quietly.
-np: recursive download / do not ascend to parent directories.
-R LIST: accept / reject file suffixes when mirroring.

examples.explanation: Downloads file.iso into the current directory with a progress bar.
Resumes an interrupted download instead of starting over.
Fetches the body to stdout quietly — useful in scripts: status=$(wget -qO- url).
Mirrors only PDF files from a documentation section without ascending to parent paths.

about: wget excels at unattended downloading: it retries on failure, supports resume (-c), can run with nohup in the background, and can mirror sites recursively. curl is better for APIs and fine-grained requests; wget is better for plain robust downloads.
useCases: Fetch files in cron jobs and scripts.
mistakes: Re-running without -c and re-downloading everything from scratch.
Recursive mirroring without -np, accidentally following links to the whole site.
warnings: Recursive downloads can fetch far more than expected; always bound them with -np, -A/-R, or --mirror with --no-parent.
distroNotes: wget is GNU software, present on virtually all Linux distributions. BusyBox includes a minimal wget variant with fewer options.
